claims.statement: Guest collaborators offer limited vendor and contractor access.
Guest collaborators are provisioned by the IdP like other managed users.
Guests may be added as organization members.
They may instead be added as repository collaborators.
Guests cannot access enterprise internal repositories outside organizations where they are members.
A regular user added to one organization automatically accesses all enterprise internal repositories, unlike the guest.
The ghec branch scopes IdP-controlled team and organization membership to EMU.
The alternative branch scopes that capability to configured SCIM provisioning.
Connecting GitHub teams to IdP groups is the described mechanism.
The guest collaborator role is only available with EMU.
Migration requires access to the GitHub enterprise.
It also requires access to the Entra tenant.
Configuring the EMU OIDC application requires sign-in as an Entra Global Administrator.
Signing in as the enterprise setup user requires an enterprise recovery code.
Schedule migration when enterprise resources are not in active use.
Users cannot access the enterprise during migration until the new application is configured.
Restoring that access also requires users to be reprovisioned.
Mixing partner IdPs for authentication and provisioning is not expressly supported.
GitHub does not test all identity-management systems.
Support may be unable to assist with mixed or untested systems.
For those systems, consult their documentation, support or other resources.
Okta plus Entra for SSO and SCIM is explicitly unsupported in either assignment order.
That combination causes provisioning attempts to receive a GitHub SCIM API error.
Sign in as SHORTCODE_admin, substituting the enterprise shortcode.
Members cannot use the SSH certificate to access organization-repository forks unless enterprise policy permits SSH CAs on user-owned repositories.
At the IdP continuation prompt, choose Use a recovery code.
Sign in using an enterprise recovery code.
The code must belong to the enterprise, not the personal user account.
The IdP application's Roles attribute can set the user's enterprise role.
User provisioning through application assignment follows authentication and provisioning configuration.
Assignment may select individual users.
Assignment may alternatively select groups.
The ghec branch names the EMU IdP application.
The alternative branch refers to the relevant IdP application.
The enterprise must have been created as an EMU enterprise when beginning Enterprise Cloud.
Under repository-collaborators, EMU renames outside collaborator as repository collaborator.
Outside-collaborator documentation generally applies to repository collaborators.
The linked role reference describes exceptions; they are not inherited as read.
Automatic sign-in redirection is labeled public preview for EMU.
That preview is subject to change.
The interface shows each member-authorized PAT for API/Git access.
It also shows each authorized SSH key.
Only the last several characters of the credential are visible.
Work with the member to identify credentials for revocation when necessary.
Revocation in this interface removes SAML authorization.
It does not delete the underlying token.
It does not delete the underlying SSH key.
A member's linked SSO identity can be viewed.
A wrongly linked identity can be revoked so the member can retry linking.
Members need an active browser SAML session for each organization's resources.
Under ghec, protected API/Git access requires a PAT or SSH key authorized for that organization.
Under ghec, enterprise owners can view and revoke member linked identities at any time.
Under ghec, enterprise owners can view and revoke member active sessions at any time.
Under ghec, enterprise owners can view and revoke member authorized credentials at any time.
The alternative branch limits that description to active SAML sessions.
In ghes, this view is enabled only with SAML and SCIM enabled.
Enterprise owners can enable centralized SAML SSO across all enterprise-owned organizations.
After enablement, SAML SSO is required for all enterprise members.
After enablement, it is also required across all owned organizations.
Members must authenticate with SAML to access their member organizations.
Enterprise owners must authenticate with SAML to access the enterprise account.
Assign the Okta application to the operator's own user.
If Configure SSO is missing, authenticate through the IdP at least once for GitHub resource access.
Repeated SAML prompts can require a longer IdP session duration.
SessionNotOnOrAfter determines when authentication returns to the IdP.
Sessions configured for two hours or less are refreshed five minutes before expiry.
Sessions lasting five minutes or less can cause an authentication loop.
Configure a minimum SAML duration of four hours to address that loop.
Authorizing a PAT requires a linked external identity.
Authorizing an SSH key likewise requires a linked external identity.
At least one IdP authentication to the SSO-enabled organization creates that link.
An authorized token or key retains authorization until one listed revocation condition occurs.
An organization owner can revoke authorization.
An enterprise owner can revoke authorization.
Under single_user_cred_revocation, owners may revoke authorizations for individual users.
Under single_user_cred_revocation, owners may revoke authorizations for all users.
Under single_user_cred_revocation, owners may revoke authorizations for a particular credential type.
Removal from the organization revokes authorization.
Changing PAT scopes revokes its authorization.
Regenerating the PAT also revokes its authorization.
PAT expiration as defined at creation ends authorization.
Choose the application label created for the enterprise account.
Select the member whose authorized credentials are to be viewed or revoked.
Select the member whose linked identity is to be viewed or revoked.
Select the member whose SAML session is to be viewed or revoked.
Read the information before choosing I understand, revoke access for this token.
Read the information before choosing Revoke external identity.
A user's first SAML authentication to an organization or enterprise can report an identity-link conflict.
The illustrative error identifies an unlinked GitHub account attempting to use an IdP identity linked to a different GitHub account.
The error directs the user to organization or enterprise owners.
For Entra, the error includes User Object ID.
GitHub calls that value External ID.
One external identity may be linked to only one GitHub user account within an organization or enterprise.
Use GraphQL to identify the account linked to the conflicting identity.
With organization-level SAML, an organization owner queries organization identities.
Filter that query by the authenticating IdP account's SAML NameID.
With enterprise-level SAML, an enterprise owner queries enterprise identities.
Filter that enterprise query by the authenticating account's SAML NameID.
After identifying a user, an enterprise owner can check whether enterprise and organization membership is still active.
Resolution depends on the identified account's continued access needs.
A support ticket is offered for resolution issues or questions.
If the conflicting account no longer needs access, remove its membership.
Proper removal is expected to remove the linked SAML identity.
It is also expected to remove an organization-level linked SCIM identity if one exists.
With SCIM-managed organization membership, deprovision through the IdP rather than GitHub UI removal.
Otherwise linked SAML/SCIM identities can remain and continue the conflict.
Without SCIM, follow the GitHub membership-removal procedure.
Also remove application access at the IdP.
If the conflicting user still needs access, changing their linked identity is one resolution.
Having the failing user authenticate with a different IdP identity is the other resolution.
To change an identity with SCIM-managed organization membership, deprovision then reprovision at the IdP.
Unassigning then reassigning the app user is the offered example.
Deprovisioning removes that GitHub account from the organization.
It also removes the linked SAML/SCIM identity.
Reprovisioning creates a new pending organization invitation.
It also creates a new unlinked SCIM identity.
The user can then sign in with their GitHub account.
They authenticate through SAML and link the new IdP identity.
Those steps are intended to align the SAML and SCIM identities with the GitHub organization account.
Without SCIM organization membership, revoke the linked identity using the linked procedures.
Enterprise-level SAML also uses that linked-identity revocation alternative.
If no conflicting GitHub account is found, revoke the stale external identity.
With SCIM organization membership, remove the stale unlinked identity through the IdP.
Unassigning the user from the IdP app is the example.
If the IdP does not send the proper SCIM call, the identity remains.
That persistence may continue the authentication error.
Without SCIM, the specified organization or enterprise people/USERNAME/sso URL supports revocation.
Replace USERNAME with the failing user's GitHub username.
Replace ORGANIZATION or ENTERPRISE with the appropriate account identifier.
The organization URL template is https://github.com/orgs/ORGANIZATION/people/USERNAME/sso.
The enterprise URL template is https://github.com/enterprises/ENTERPRISE/people/USERNAME/sso.
Disabling SAML SSO preserves members' personal access tokens.
Disabling SAML SSO preserves members' SSH keys.
Disabling SAML SSO preserves members' OAuth App authorizations.
Disabling SAML SSO preserves members' GitHub App authorizations.
Their existing SSO credential authorizations are not revoked.
Re-enabling SSO causes identity relinking at next sign-in.
Existing tokens do not need reauthorization after re-enablement.
Existing SSH keys likewise do not need reauthorization.
Excessive clock difference between GitHub and the IdP can cause Current time is earlier than NotBefore condition.
The source identifies self-hosted IdPs as a common setting for this difference.
Under ghes, use the same NTP source for appliance and IdP if possible.
For that error, ensure the appliance clock is NTP-synchronized in ghes.
The alternative branch checks the IdP clock instead.
Under ghes, chronyc on the administrative shell can synchronize time immediately; no command was run.
For ADFS, set NotBeforeSkew to one minute for GitHub.
Zero NotBeforeSkew can make even millisecond clock differences cause authentication failures.
SSO lets organization owners control and secure organization-resource access.
Enterprise owners likewise control and secure that access.
Choose the pencil beside current signature and digest methods under the public certificate.
The authored image alt describes an orange-highlighted pencil for signature/digest settings, without image inspection.
Choose the issuer's hashing algorithm in Signature Method.
Choose the issuer's hashing algorithm in Digest Method as well.
In ghec, organization SAML SSO requires Enterprise Cloud.
The ghec branch discusses IAM under EMU.
The alternative discusses IdP-based GHES IAM.
SAML secures access to enterprise resources.
SCIM automatically creates user accounts following IdP changes.
SCIM also manages enterprise access following IdP changes.
GitHub teams can synchronize with IdP groups.
An organization-linked identity requires authorized PATs for that organization even without enforced SSO.
That condition also requires authorized SSH keys.
Past SSO authentication creates the linked identity unless an organization or enterprise owner later revokes it.
Under ghec, enterprise SCIM requires an account created for EMU.
A non-EMU enterprise needing SCIM must configure organization-level rather than enterprise-level SAML.

Choose Add Integration.
Expand Applications in the Okta dashboard.
Choose Applications in that menu.
Choose the label of the organization's Enterprise Cloud application.
Choose Browse App Catalog.
Choose Configure API Integration.
Use the sidebar Applications dropdown to choose Applications.
Choose Edit beside Provisioning to App.
Enable Create Users.
Enable Update User Attributes.
Enable Deactivate Users.
Save the provisioning settings.
Select Enable API integration.
Choose Provisioning under the application name.
Choose Save.
Sign in to the Okta account.
Choose Sign on under the application name.
Choose View Setup Instructions under SIGN ON METHODS.

Enter the code in Recovery Code.
Choose Verify.
Choose Revoke beside the target credential.
Choose Revoke beside the target session.
Choose Revoke beside the linked identity.
Choose SAML identity linked in the sidebar.
Retrieve ExternalIdentity for each member through GraphQL.
Inspect the member's Authorized credentials.
Inspect the member's Active SAML sessions.
Inspect the member's Linked SSO identity.
Audit organization users to avoid syncing errors.
That audit should confirm SAML-enabled users.
It should also confirm linked SCIM identities.
Outside collaborators are exempt from SSO authentication in this context.
A personal-account owner chooses whether email is public.
A hidden email cannot be viewed by the consuming administrator.
Without SAML, GitHub cannot display external identity information such as NameID.
NameID is typically an email address, not invariably so.
After use, mark the recovery code invalid.
A used recovery code cannot be reused.
Each recovery code is usable once.
Codes must be used in consecutive order.
A recovery code grants access for 24 hours.
Users removed by SAML enforcement can rejoin through SAML authentication.
Public-repository viewing the repository overview and files does not require IdP authentication.
Public-repository forking does not require IdP authentication.
Public-repository Git read operations such as cloning does not require IdP authentication.
Viewing public-repository issues requires authentication in this SAML context.
Viewing public-repository pull requests requires authentication in this SAML context.
Viewing public-repository projects requires authentication in this SAML context.
Viewing public-repository releases requires authentication in this SAML context.
Organization SAML users continue signing into personal GitHub.com accounts.
Accessing most organization resources redirects the user to the IdP.
Successful IdP authentication redirects back to GitHub.
SAML does not replace normal GitHub sign-in.
Unless EMU is used, a personal account is linked to an external IdP identity.
Disabling SAML SSO removes all linked external identities from GitHub.
With ghes JIT provisioning, removing an IdP user also requires manual suspension on the appliance.
Without that suspension, access-token authentication remains possible.
Without suspension, SSH-key authentication also remains possible.
The authored alt describes an orange-highlighted SAML identity linked entry for octocat, without visual asset review.
Membership in a SAML-enforcing organization can require IdP authentication before OAuth App authorization.
GitHub does not support SAML Single Logout.
Terminate an active SAML session by logging out directly at the IdP.
SAML 2.0 implementation is the general supported IdP standard.
GitHub officially supports and internally tests AD FS for SAML.
GitHub officially supports and internally tests Microsoft Entra ID formerly Azure AD for SAML.
GitHub officially supports and internally tests Okta for SAML.
GitHub officially supports and internally tests OneLogin for SAML.
GitHub officially supports and internally tests PingOne for SAML.
GitHub officially supports and internally tests Shibboleth for SAML.
Enterprise SAML enablement has special considerations when its organizations already use SAML.
Changing reinvitation settings does not alter pending invitations.
Invitations created while reinvitation was allowed can still restore past members after the option is disallowed.
The configuration test uses SP-initiated authentication.
That test must succeed before saving SAML settings.
Leaving Require SAML SSO authentication for all members unchecked allows testing without affecting organization members.
Organization-level identity access is available to organization owners.
An organization-owner PAT can access those identities with read:org or admin:org.
An organization-installed App installation token can access them with read or write member access.
Enterprise identities require an enterprise-owner PAT with read:enterprise or admin:enterprise.
GitHub Apps cannot access enterprise-level external identities.
That App restriction includes enterprise SAML identities on Enterprise Cloud with personal user accounts.
Enforced SAML requires all organization members to authenticate at the IdP for organization resources.
IdP reauthentication is periodically required for organization-resource access.
The default login period is 24 hours unless the IdP specifies otherwise.
Periodic login limits access duration and requires renewed identification.
Active SSO sessions can be viewed in security settings.
Active SSO sessions can also be managed there.
By default, app assignment or unassignment at the IdP does not automatically communicate with GitHub.
SAML JIT provisioning occurs at the user's first IdP-authenticated resource sign-in.
In fpt or ghec, JIT provisions resource access.
In the alternative branch, JIT creates a user account.
Manual notification may be needed when granting access.
JIT offboarding in fpt or ghec requires manual access deprovisioning.
In the alternative branch, offboarding requires manual account deactivation.
SCIM is offered instead of JIT for automatic response to assignment or unassignment.
The ghec branch names provisioning or deprovisioning.
The ghes branch names account creation or suspension.
The fpt or ghec branch describes access to enterprise-owned organizations.
The alternative describes accounts with granted or denied appliance access.
Under ghes, the source calls SCIM preview and subject to change.
Nested scim-for-ghes-public-beta selects public versus private preview wording.
With organization SCIM, membership changes should originate at the IdP.
Manual invitations can fail to link the GitHub account correctly to SCIM.
That missing link can prevent later SCIM deprovisioning.
Manual removals leave stale linked identities.
Those stale identities can obstruct rejoining.
Organization SCIM requires a third-party-owned OAuth App.
The App must be authorized by a specific GitHub user.
The App acts on behalf of that user.
If the last authorizing user leaves or is removed, SCIM stops working.
Create a dedicated configuration account to avoid that dependency.
The dedicated account must be an organization owner.
It consumes a license.
Authentication must be configured before provisioning.
That setup requires configuration on the identity-management system.
It also requires configuration on GitHub.
Under ghec, assign no more than 1,000 users per hour to the IdP SCIM integration to avoid the GitHub rate limit.
With group assignment, add no more than 1,000 users per group per hour.
Exceeding those thresholds can make provisioning fail with a rate-limit error.
Check IdP logs for rate-limited provisioning or push failures.
The response to failed provisioning depends on the IdP.
Under ghes, a site administrator may have enabled instance API limits.
Exceeding those limits can make provisioning fail with a rate-limit error.
Check IdP logs for those failures.
The GHES failed-attempt response likewise depends on the IdP.
The containing SCIM implementation cannot be used with an enterprise account.
It cannot be used with an EMU organization.
An EMU enterprise must use a different SCIM implementation.
Without EMU, enterprise-level SCIM is unavailable in this context.
Enterprise administrators with CLI access can export the full SCIM identity CSV.
ghe-scim-identities-csv is the named export tool; it was not executed.
The containing endpoints provision Enterprise Cloud enterprise accounts through SCIM.
That operation is available only for EMU.
Non-EMU organization access provisioning is directed to a different endpoint reference.
Test provisioning isolated from production IdP data.
Also isolate testing from production GitHub data.
Import Groups is unsupported.
Checking or unchecking Import Groups has no configuration effect.
SAML NameID must match SCIM userName for each user.
That match links SAML-authenticated users to their provisioned SCIM identity.
The containing operation provisions organization access on Enterprise Cloud.
It is unavailable for EMU.
EMU SCIM provisioning is directed to the enterprise-admin reference.
The containing group update operation records external_group.update.
Changing the group name records external_group.update_display_name.
Adding a user records external_group.add_member.
Removing a user records external_group.remove_member.
A successful request records external_group.scim_api_success.
A failed request records external_group.scim_api_failure.
Additional events depend on whether the user is already an organization member where the IdP-linked team resides.
The operation records external_identity.update except during soft deprovisioning or reprovisioning.
Adding enterprise_owner records business.add_admin.
Adding billing_manager records business.add_billing_manager.
Removing enterprise_owner records business.remove_admin.
Removing billing_manager records business.remove_billing_manager.
Successful requests record external_identity.scim_api_success.
Failed requests record external_identity.scim_api_failure.
Provisioning users through the REST API requires an identity-management system supporting SCIM 2.0.
Provisioning groups through that API also requires SCIM 2.0.
The Okta product must support SCIM.
Consult Okta documentation or support for that product capability.
